about: Box sizes, in bytes. plaintext is the most a box of that size holds; padded is the plaintext after Katzenpost's padding (a big endian u32 length, the plaintext, zeros); ciphertext is the padded plaintext sealed by BACAP; write_query is a mesh replica's write query (type byte, box ID, signature, ciphertext); channel_message is it as one Channel message (6 byte envelope, 4 byte frame header) and link_request as a Link request (msgpack of [time, path hash, query]). mesh, a writer's default on Reticulum, is the largest multiple of 16 whose channel_message and link_request leave headroom bytes of one Link packet (link_mdu) spare; mixnet is Katzenpost's. Only the payload differs: box IDs and signatures are the same size in each. A reader takes a box of any allowed size: the named ones, its writer's own and configured extras, each within min..max. mixed_stream is one stream, read with read_cap from its first index on, whose boxes are of different sizes, extra_sizes among them: they hold one substream, whose message is assembled. Generated by scripts/gen_box_sizes.py.
